## Mapped: Data Center Capacity Around the World

This was originally posted on our Voronoi app. Download the app for free on iOS or Android and discover incredible data-driven charts from a variety of trusted sources.

### Key Takeaways

- Global installed data center capacity stood at 122.2 gigawatts (GW) in 2024.
- Together, the U.S. and China account for 70% of the global total.
- The European Union follows next, with 11.9 GW in capacity.

Today, the U.S. leads globally in data center capacity by a wide margin.

Driven by hyperscalers like AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure, billions in investment are supporting foundational AI models. As this momentum continues, these tech giants are expected to remain key drivers of global data center growth.

This graphic shows data center capacity by region, based on data from the IEA.

## The Global Concentration of Data Center Infrastructure

Below, we show data center capacity worldwide in 2024: ​​ 

| Country | Installed Data Center Capacity in Gigawatts |
| --- | --- |
| U.S. | 53.7 |
| China | 31.9 |
| EU | 11.9 |
| Japan and Korea | 6.6 |
| Other Asia Pacific | 3.1 |
| Other North America | 1.5 |
| UK | 2.6 |
| Africa | 1.5 |
| Australia and New Zealand | 1.6 |
| India | 3.6 |
| Eurasia | 1.2 |
| Middle East | 1.1 |
| Other Central and South America | 1.4 |
| Brazil | 0.6 |
| Total | 122.2 |

With 53.7 GW of installed capacity, the U.S. accounts for 44% of the global total.

Given the intensifying demand for data centers, hyperscalers are facing infrastructure constraints. New data centers set to be built out by 2028 are completely booked, and Northern Virginia faces power capacity shortages causing project delays.

Meanwhile, public and private entities in China have invested billions in data centers, but an estimated 80% of new infrastructure stands unused.

As we can see, the EU trails behind with 11.9 GW of capacity. Still, electricity demand from data centers is expected to surge 150% by 2035, driven by approximately $231 billion in AI-related investment aimed at tripling capacity by 2032.

To learn more about data centers from a capacity perspective, check out this graphic on historical growth since 2005.

## Which Countries Spend the Most Time Playing Video Games?

### Key Takeaways

- The Philippines leads the ranking, with internet users spending an average of 11 hours and 14 minutes gaming each week.
- Five of the top 10 markets are in the Americas, including Brazil, Mexico, the United States, Chile, and Argentina.
- All five East Asian markets surveyed, including Japan, China, and South Korea, rank below the worldwide average for weekly gaming time.

This visualization ranks 54 countries and territories by weekly gaming time using data from GWI’s Q2 2025 research, published in the Digital 2026 Global Overview Report. The figures cover internet users aged 16 and older and include mobile, console, and computer gaming.

Together, Google and YouTube received 168.9 billion visits, compared with 91.3 billion across the other 38 websites in the ranking. In other words, Alphabet’s two leading platforms generated nearly twice as many visits as the rest of the top 40 combined, including major social networks, shopping sites, streaming services, and AI tools.

Other search engines draw substantial traffic but remain much smaller, with Bing receiving 2.3 billion monthly visits and DuckDuckGo 2.2 billion.

## ChatGPT Joins the Internet’s Biggest Platforms

ChatGPT’s position among the top five websites puts an AI assistant alongside some of the internet’s most established social media platforms. Its 8.2 billion monthly visits place it between Facebook and Instagram, highlighting how prominent AI tools have become in everyday web activity.

Meta’s reach extends further through WhatsApp, which ranks seventh with 4.3 billion visits. Together, Facebook, Instagram, and WhatsApp attract 23.3 billion monthly visits, giving Meta a substantial presence across social networking, photo sharing, and messaging.

Reddit, X (formerly Twitter), and TikTok are among the other major social media platforms attracting billions of monthly visits.

While ChatGPT ranks alongside established social platforms, its closest AI competitors sit much further down the list. Claude, another of the world’s most popular AI tools, ranks 21st with 1.6 billion visits, roughly one-fifth of ChatGPT’s monthly traffic.
